run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:59:39Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by chaos-mesh network fault injection. At 2026-11-17T09:59:29Z NetworkChaos otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj in namespace chaos-mesh started and its events record 'Successfully apply chaos' for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn; further NetworkChaos objects with the same prefix (5c2dr, 7rvkf, 8p7rs, hddgv, mznpj, zl9p2) repeated Started/Applied/Recovered between 09:59:29Z and 10:06:29Z. After that point checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs could no longer reach the email Service: its logs repeat 'failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' (100.67.49.77 being the email Service ClusterIP) and its only ERROR span operation is 'HTTP POST' carrying that dial-timeout description. /api/checkout then exceeded the proxy's upstream wait, so frontend-proxy logged 'POST /api/checkout ... 504 UT response_timeout' with 15001 ms upstream time and its ingress ERROR spans rose from roughly 0-2.7 per 2 minutes to 18.7-41.3 per 2 minutes, firing the alert at 09:59:39Z. Other proxy routes returned 200 in the same seconds; the email Service still had two ready endpoint addresses, email emitted no ERROR spans, and all otel-demo pods were Running and ready with 0 restarts, which argues against an email application failure, a pod crash or a proxy-internal defect. The chaos-mesh Schedule that appears to spawn these experiments could not be read, so the driving schedule and partition parameters remain unverified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ERROR span count (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) reached 218.4 per rolling 21 minutes at 10:17:39Z; both of its ERROR operations are on span_name=ingress (218.4) while span_name='router frontend egress' stayed 0, and total spans on the service fell from 27881.7 to 14963.3 per 21 minutes over the same period.

The surge is sharp and late: frontend-proxy's 2-minute ERROR span increase was 1.33 in the window ending 10:00:39Z, jumped to 28 in the window ending 10:01:39Z, and stayed between 18.7 and 41.3 per 2 minutes through 10:09:39Z, whereas the preceding 09:41:39-10:00:39Z period showed only 0-2.7 per 2 minutes.

The failing frontend-proxy spans are HTTP 504s: sampled spans of service frontend-proxy on operation 'ingress' carry status_tags http.status_code=504 and otel.status_code=ERROR with roughly 15 s durations, and their child spans are load-generator 'POST' spans that also carry error=true and http.status_code=504.

frontend-proxy's own access log shows the 504 mechanism on the checkout route: at container timestamp 2026-11-17T09:59:54.785Z it logged 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout - "-" 395 24 15001' (15001 ms upstream time, Envoy response_timeout), while neighbouring /api/products, /api/cart, /api/recommendations and / requests in the same seconds returned 200 via_upstream.

The dependency failure sits in checkout's call to email: checkout's only ERROR span operation is 'HTTP POST' (100.94 per 21 minutes at 10:17:39Z, not present before 10:01:39Z) and the sampled span carries otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'.

checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs logged 97 matching error lines between 10:03:02Z and 10:07:18Z, all of the form 'failed to send order confirmation to "<address>": failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'.

The address checkout cannot reach is the email Service: in namespace otel-demo the Service 'email' has ClusterIP 100.67.49.77 and port 8080, and its Endpoints object lists two ready addresses, 100.96.2.7 and 100.96.3.218, with no notReadyAddresses.

Events name the fault injector: NetworkChaos otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj in namespace chaos-mesh emitted Started at 09:59:29Z and 'Applied - Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w', '...otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn' and 'otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs', then TimeUp at 10:00:24Z and Recovered; NetworkChaos objects with the same name prefix (jdmmj, hddgv, mznpj, zl9p2, 7rvkf, 8p7rs, 5c2dr) repeated Started/Applied/Recovered cycles at 09:59:29, 10:00:29, 10:01:29, 10:02:29, 10:03:29, 10:04:29, 10:05:29 and 10:06:29Z.

Event grouping over the window shows 24 NetworkChaos/Applied, 21 NetworkChaos/Recovered and 8 NetworkChaos/Started events in chaos-mesh, 45 PodNetworkChaos/Updated events in otel-demo, plus 8 Schedule/Spawned and 8 Schedule/Updated events in chaos-mesh, indicating a chaos-mesh Schedule spawns these experiments.

No pod-level crash accompanies the fault: every pod in namespace otel-demo, including checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59, was phase Running, ready=true and restartCount 0 at query time.

The email service shows no error status of its own: its only traces_span_metrics_calls_total series in the window is status_code=STATUS_CODE_UNSET (falling from 2927.5 to 1227.3 per 21 minutes, i.e. reduced volume rather than errors), no ERROR series exists for email, and frontend, accounting and payment report 0 ERROR spans throughout.

The hypothesis that frontend-proxy itself is defective (bad routing or self-inflicted timeout) was rejected: its error spans are confined to operation 'ingress' with 504 on the /api/checkout route, its log shows other routes returning 200 via_upstream in the same seconds, and the abort is 'response_timeout' after 15001 ms waiting on the upstream frontend, so the proxy is reporting an upstream stall.

The hypothesis that the email service application itself failed was rejected: the email Service had two ready endpoint addresses (100.96.2.7, 100.96.3.218), both email pods were Running/ready with 0 restarts, email emits no ERROR spans, and checkout's symptom is a TCP 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' to the Service ClusterIP, which fits dropped packets rather than an unresponsive listener.

Events from the data-recorders namespace (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, 7 Job/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet creations, PVC provisioning, Pod FailedScheduling, PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete) were considered and rejected as this cause, because they occur in a different namespace and no evidence ties them to the frontend-proxy/checkout/email failure path.

The recurring NetworkChaos instances are most likely produced by a chaos-mesh Schedule, because Schedule/Spawned and Schedule/Updated events exist in chaos-mesh, so the persistent fault may be driven by that Schedule rather than by a single NetworkChaos object; the Schedule's name and spec and the NetworkChaos selector/direction/loss parameters could not be read with the available tools.

Suspend or delete the chaos-mesh NetworkChaos/Schedule experiments named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-* in namespace chaos-mesh, then confirm that checkout's 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' log lines stop and frontend-proxy's ingress 504/ERROR spans on /api/checkout return to their prior background level.

If the partition experiment is intentional, suppress or annotate RequestErrorRate for service frontend-proxy during the chaos window and shorten checkout's email HTTP timeout below frontend-proxy's 15001 ms Envoy response_timeout so that a blocked email dependency surfaces as a fast error instead of a proxy 504.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate, with type=alert and with match {service_name="frontend-proxy"} each returned no rules (status no_data), so the rule expression, its 'for' duration and the alert's reported 0.2444 error-rate value are unverified.

NetworkChaos and Schedule specs (pod selector, direction, loss/partition percentage, duration) are not readable: those kinds were not available, and the networkpolicies query returned no objects (status no_data), so whether the fault is a full partition or partial packet loss is unknown.

Events cover only 2026-11-17T09:59:29Z to 10:06:29Z (retention-limited), so chaos cycles before 09:59:29Z and after 10:06:29Z are unknown; the 0-2.7 ERROR spans per 2 minutes seen before 09:59:39Z remain unattributed background.

Metric samples begin at 09:41:39Z (source_start_at) even though the query window starts 08:59:39Z, so only about 18 minutes of pre-surge baseline exist and longer-term error-rate behaviour is unknown.

Log reads end early: checkout logs were read only through 10:07:18Z, frontend-proxy's 4 MiB read limit cut at 09:59:57Z, and follow-up log queries for 10:12:00-10:17:49Z (frontend-proxy '504', checkout 'i/o timeout') returned no lines (status no_data), so behaviour after about 10:08Z could not be read from logs.
The email container produced no log lines at all in 09:40:00-10:17:49Z (status no_data, lines_read 0), so the email side of the failed calls could not be inspected at application level.
Trace data is a sampled view and trace span counts are not unique request counts, so the exact number of failed /api/checkout requests is unknown.
No change-history integration is available, so who or what created the chaos Schedule and whether the experiment was scheduled for this incident could not be verified.

An http_server_request_duration_seconds_count query for service_name=frontend-proxy on the otel-demo target returned no series, so the error-rate denominator used by the alert could not be reproduced.
next_steps: A human with chaos-mesh read access should inspect the Schedule and NetworkChaos objects named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-* in namespace chaos-mesh to confirm the selector, direction and loss parameters and who created them.
Retrieve the actual RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Prometheus rule files or Alertmanager configuration to confirm the expression and threshold behind the 0.2444 value.
After any chaos cleanup, verify recovery by watching frontend-proxy ingress 504/ERROR spans on /api/checkout and checkout's 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' log lines.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then.
